name: Page Industries Ltd
about: Incorporated in 1995, Page Industries Limited is the exclusive licensee of JOCKEY International Inc. for manufacturing, distribution, and marketing of the JOCKEY® brand in India, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, Nepal, and the UAE. Page Industries is also the exclusive licensee of Speedo International Ltd. for the manufacturing, marketing, and distribution of the Speedo brand in India.

statements.text: Revenue compounded 13.1% a year over 5 years (FY21→FY26); profit after tax 17.5%.
EBITDA margin expanded 340 bps over 5 years (18.6% → 22.0%).
Revenue growth accelerated from 6% to 12% YoY over the last 4 quarters.
Over 5 years: ₹3,170 cr of profit, ₹3,403 cr of operating cash — conversion 1.07x.

ledger.quote: our annual outlook on EBITDA margin will still be within this 19% to 21%
ledger.statement: Annual EBITDA margin within 19-21% for FY27
ledger.speaker: Deepanjan Bandyopadhyay

check.basis: FY27 EBITDA margin to date (2 of 4 quarters)

ledger.evidence: Computed check: the FY27-to-date (2 of 4 quarters) EBITDA margin is 20.6%, inside 19-21%. Quarterly margins were 20.4% in Q1 and 20.8% in Q2 (F:margin_last4_pct). Management said input costs had largely normalised by end-June (C3), but Q1 included a low-cost inventory benefit (C2).

ledger.quote: the annual goal remains unchanged, which is to aim for a double-digit growth in volume
ledger.statement: Volume growth of double digits (10% or more) for FY27
ledger.speaker: Karthik Yathindra
ledger.evidence: Q1 FY27 volume grew 5.7% (C1), about half the double-digit target, and management reaffirmed the goal on that same call. There is no Q2 FY27 volume figure. Q2 revenue grew 11.5% YoY (F:rev_yoy_last_q_pct), but that includes price/mix and the Q1 billing shortfall rolling into Q2 (G3), so H2 volume probably needs to grow in the low-to-mid teens.

ledger.quote: largely yes, majority of this should be reported in quarter two
ledger.statement: Majority of the Q1 billing shortfall to be reported as revenue in Q2FY27
ledger.speaker: Karthik Yathindra
ledger.evidence: Q2 FY27 revenue growth accelerated to 11.5% YoY from 7.8% in Q1 (F:rev_yoy_last4_pct), which is consistent with the shortfall being billed in Q2. However, the inputs give neither the size of the shortfall nor Q2 commentary, so 'majority' cannot be confirmed.

ledger.quote: the goal is by end of this year or latest first quarter of next year, all of the distributors in our network should be on DMS
ledger.statement: All distributors on DMS by end of year, latest Q1 of next year
ledger.horizon: end of this year, latest Q1 next year
ledger.speaker: Karthik Yathindra
ledger.evidence: Deadline is year-end, or Q1 of next year at the latest. As of Q1 FY27 only 'a very small portion' of distributors were on DMS (C4), and no later update is in the inputs, so the full rollout has to happen within two to three quarters.
ledger.actual_text: Very small portion of distributors on DMS at Q1 FY27 (C4)

ledger.quote: We're still confident that we will operate between 19% to 21%.
ledger.statement: EBITDA margin range of 19-21%, targeted for FY27
ledger.speaker: Karthik Yathindra

check.basis: FY27 EBITDA margin to date (2 of 4 quarters)

ledger.evidence: Same FY27 band, held unchanged from Q3 FY26 through Q1 FY27 (drift: held). The computed H1 FY27 margin is 20.6%.

ledger.quote: what we will be targeting going forward is to try and maintain this momentum of double digit as we take on the new year
ledger.speaker: Karthik Yathindra
ledger.evidence: Held in Q1 FY27 (drift: held, G2), but the first FY27 quarter delivered 5.7% volume growth (C1) and no Q2 volume is disclosed.

ledger.quote: So over the year, I think we are expecting we should be getting around INR40 crores to INR50 crores of subsidy
ledger.statement: Subsidy income of INR40-50 crore expected over FY27
ledger.speaker: Deepanjan B
ledger.evidence: FY27 subsidy income, period not over, with no subsidy figure in the inputs. At INR 40-50 crore it would equal 5-7% of TTM PAT of INR 765 crore (F:ttm_pat_cr).

ledger.quote: We target to take that up to close to 5% in the next year.
ledger.statement: Target of close to 5% next year for the metric discussed (the referent is not clear from the passage)
ledger.speaker: Karthik Yathindra
ledger.evidence: The ledger itself notes that the metric the 'close to 5%' refers to is not identifiable from the passage.

ledger.quote: we are maintaining a similar range of 19% to 21%
ledger.statement: EBITDA margin of 19-21% for the coming year (FY27) and as a long-term range
ledger.speaker: Karthik Yathindra

check.basis: FY27 EBITDA margin to date (2 of 4 quarters)

ledger.evidence: Computed check: 20.6% for H1 FY27, inside the band. It was also framed as a long-term range, and TTM margin is 21.2% (F:ttm_margin_pct), just above the top.

ledger.quote: that is unlikely to be maintained going forward
ledger.statement: Current elevated EBITDA margin of about 22% not expected to be sustained
ledger.speaker: Deepanjan Bandyopadhyay
ledger.evidence: The margin was 22.9% in Q3 FY26 when management said it would not be sustained, and it has since been 20.8%, 20.4% and 20.8% (F:margin_last4_pct), so the call was right.
ledger.actual_text: Margin normalised to 20.4-20.8% in the next three quarters

ledger.quote: we should still be targeting that double-digit growth
ledger.statement: Aspiration to return to double-digit revenue growth, no timeline given
ledger.speaker: Karthik Yathindra
ledger.evidence: No timeline. Revenue grew in double digits in Q4 FY26 (14.1%) and Q2 FY27 (11.5%) but not in Q3 FY26 (5.6%) or Q1 FY27 (7.8%) (F:rev_yoy_last4_pct). It has been reached but not sustained, and three-year revenue CAGR is 3.6%.

ledger.quote: Our intent, I think I mentioned this in the past as well, is to reach a near double-digit growth in terms of performance by the company
ledger.statement: Aspire to near double-digit company growth; no date given
ledger.speaker: Karthik Yathindra
ledger.evidence: Quarterly YoY revenue growth over the last four quarters averages about 9.8% (5.6%, 14.1%, 7.8%, 11.5%; F:rev_yoy_last4_pct), which counts as 'near double-digit'. This is a trailing-four-quarter read, not a full fiscal year, and it follows a three-year CAGR of 3.6%.
ledger.actual_text: About 9.8% average YoY revenue growth over the last four quarters

ledger.quote: And as we keep telling, we are very happy with the 19% to 21% EBITDA. And we are very confident we can be in that range
ledger.speaker: V.S. Ganesh
ledger.evidence: The last four quarterly margins were 22.9%, 20.8%, 20.4% and 20.8% (F:margin_last4_pct): three inside the band and one above it, with none below 19%.

ledger.quote: We plan to spend around INR140 crores in FY '26
ledger.statement: FY26 capex of about INR 140 crore
ledger.speaker: Deepanjan B.
ledger.evidence: FY26 has ended, but the facts contain no capex figure. Five-year FCF of INR 816 crore (F:fcf_5y_cr) cannot isolate FY26 spend.

ledger.quote: for the year, we generally maintain a 4%, 4.5% budget
ledger.statement: Marketing budget of 4-4.5% for the year
ledger.speaker: V.S. Ganesh
ledger.evidence: FY26 has ended, but the inputs contain no advertising or marketing spend.

tones.label: confident
tones.why: Management says "the annual goal remains unchanged" and reaffirms the 19-21% EBITDA margin range.

tones.label: cautious
tones.why: Management is aggressive on demand but guides margins to 19-21%, below the 22% delivered in FY26, and flags input cost inflation and technology investment as pressures.

tones.label: mixed
tones.why: Management is confident the recovery is steady and double-digit growth remains the target, but says it is difficult to put a timeline on it (p8-43-1, p14-86-1).

tones.label: mixed
tones.why: Management admits first-half revenue has been subpar against internal targets, but is confident about the 19-21% EBITDA margin band and the capex and marketing budgets.

context.speaker: Deepanjan B.
context.text: Thank you, V.S. ji. Good afternoon, everyone. I will now provide an overview of the company’s financial performance for quarter one FY27. In quarter one, revenue was INR14,204 million, Page 3 of 15 Page Industries Limited August 13, 2026 which is a 7.9% growth year-on-year. Sales volume in the quarter was 61.9 million pieces, growing by 5.7% year-on-year. EBITDA for the period was INR2,890 million, which has declined by 1.9% year-on-year. EBITDA margin was 20.3%, while EBITDA margin was within our planned range of 19% to 21%, a stronger EBITDA margin of 22.4% in Q1 FY26 due to the stable input cost then resulted in the decline in EBITDA in the current quarter. Profit after tax for the quarter was INR1,928 million, declining by around 4% year-on-year. Inventory days was 66 in the end of quarter one, as against 73 days in the beginning of the quarter. Net working capital, days was around 54 days as against 56 days in the beginning of the quarter. With that, we can now take up the queries.

context.speaker: Avi Mehta
context.text: Perfect. And just on the input cost bit. See, I mean, if I recollect there was some low-cost inventory benefit that we had in this quarter despite that gross margin did come under pressure. Wanted to just appreciate how are we placed now? And should we see sequential margins kind of more or less now improving or is there some pressure in the near-term that we should kind of build in? And in turn, how do you see the full year EBITDA margin guidance? Would you retain that at 19% to 21%? Thank you.

context.speaker: Deepanjan Bandyopadhyay
context.text: Okay, so mid of last quarter, yes, we did see inflationary conditions in the input cost, especially cotton and nylon and even synthetic packaging. In fact, fabrics also went up and as well as any synthetic products that we are buying, which is petroleum based. There also there was a significant escalation. So while we did pre-positioning of supplies, we couldn't fully absorb the extreme increases that happened. But yes, end of June and even now, the situation has to a large extent normalized and going forward we expect things to be stable. Of course, if there is again an escalation in the Middle East situation, it can happen differently. But as of now, we expect things should be stable. And with that, our annual outlook on EBITDA margin will still be within this 19% to 21%.

Yeah. So the DMS is underway, but we've not yet completely moved ahead. It's still a very small portion of distributors who are on DMS today. But the goal is by end of this year or latest first quarter of next year, all of the distributors in our network should be on DMS and then give it about a quarter more to stabilize as a tool and thereafter you will start seeing efficiencies coming into the system.

business.what_it_does: Indian apparel company selling garments by the piece (61.9 million pieces in Q1 FY27) through a distributor network that is moving onto a distributor management system (DMS). Main inputs are cotton, nylon, fabrics and petroleum-based synthetics. Q1 FY27 revenue was INR 14,204 million; TTM revenue is INR 5,500 crore.

segments.name: Apparel (single reported business in the inputs)
segments.comment: No segment split in the inputs. Q1 FY27 volume grew 5.7% YoY against 7.9% revenue growth; EBITDA margin was 20.3%.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: The FY27 EBITDA margin will be within 19-21%, held across three calls, with input costs 'to a large extent normalized' after the Q1 spike (G1, G5, G9, C3).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: The H1 FY27 margin is 20.6%, with Q2 at 20.8% recovering from 20.4% in Q1. It is still 90 bps below 21.7% in Q2 FY26.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Annual goal 'remains unchanged' at double-digit volume growth (G2, G6).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: Q1 FY27 volume grew 5.7% (C1). Q2 revenue grew 11.5%, but that includes price and the Q1 billing spillover (G3). Three-year revenue CAGR is 3.6%, so double-digit volume would be a break from trend.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Growth is returning to double digits (G11, G12).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: Revenue grew 11.5% in Q2 FY27, but PAT grew only 4.1% because the margin slipped 90 bps YoY. Over three years PAT grew 10.2% a year on 3.6% revenue growth, carried by a 370 bps margin expansion that the self-imposed 19-21% band now caps.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Working capital is tightening: inventory fell from 73 to 66 days and net working capital from 56 to 54 days in Q1 FY27 (C1).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: The cash conversion cycle fell from 240 days three years ago to 138 days. Five-year CFO/PAT is 1.07 and FCF is INR 816 crore.

bull.point: Margin guidance is reliable: H1 FY27 EBITDA margin is 20.6% within a 19-21% band held for three calls, TTM margin is 21.2% and ROCE is 64%.
Revenue is re-accelerating: +11.5% YoY in Q2 FY27 after +7.8% in Q1, and +14.1% in Q4 FY26. This is consistent with the Q1 billing shortfall being billed in Q2.

Cash release from working capital: the cash cycle fell from 240 to 138 days over three years, inventory days fell from 73 to 66 in Q1 FY27, and five-year CFO/PAT is 1.07. A full DMS rollout targeted by end-year to Q1 next year is meant to add distribution efficiency.

bear.point: Volume is the gap: Q1 FY27 volume grew 5.7% against a reaffirmed double-digit FY27 target, no Q2 volume is disclosed, and three-year revenue CAGR is only 3.6%.

Earnings are lagging sales: Q2 PAT grew 4.1% on 11.5% revenue growth as margin fell from 21.7% to 20.8%, and Q1 EBITDA fell 1.9% with PAT down about 4%. With the margin band capped at 19-21%, the 370 bps of margin expansion that powered three-year PAT growth will not repeat.

Input costs are exposed: cotton, nylon, fabric and petroleum-based inputs spiked in Q1 and pre-buying 'couldn't fully absorb' the increase. Management flags a renewed Middle East escalation as a risk, and INR 40-50 crore of expected subsidy (5-7% of TTM PAT) is also propping profit.

questions: What was Q2 FY27 volume growth, and how much of the 11.5% revenue growth was the Q1 billing shortfall rolling into Q2? What H2 volume growth do you need to reach double digits for FY27?
With the EBITDA margin capped at 19-21%, where does mid-teens PAT growth come from if volume stays at 5-8%? How much of FY27 EBITDA depends on the INR 40-50 crore subsidy?

What share of distributors is on DMS today against 'all' by Q1 next year at the latest? And what does the 'close to 5%' target from Q4 FY26 refer to, and where did FY26 marketing spend land against the 4-4.5% budget?
